description: Retry timing and attempt counts (sections 7.2, 7.5 and 3.5), run with the fake transport and fake clock, every wait in seconds. retryAfter cases answer a 503 carrying retryAfter (null for no header), then a 200, at now with maxRetryDelay: the SDK waits exactly seconds (wait), waits a random time within retry 0's backoff bounds (backoff), or fails at once with the 503's ApiError (fail). backoff cases give the full-jitter bounds before retry n, counted from 0, and limits the most attempts a call makes. attempts cases build the client credential names (a server key, a fixed customer token, or a token provider answering tokens in order, each valid for an hour from now), make request with the transport giving answers in order, and compare the attempts made, the provider's calls, the bounds of each wait between attempts and the result. A GET request is check(feature) on the customer its path names (me on the in-app client); the POST request is recordUsage(body.feature, body.amount, { idempotencyKey }) with the request's idempotencyKey. An answer is { status, headers?, body? }, where body is JSON and an answer without one has an empty body, or a failure: connection (no answer arrives), timeout (the attempt runs past its timeout) or cut-off (the transport sends a 200's status, its Content-Type application/json header and the first part of a JSON body, then fails the body read with its own I/O or connection error, which is a ConnectionError and retried like one; a complete body that is not valid JSON is a different failure, invalid_response, never retried).

cases.name: absent
cases.why: Without Retry-After the SDK waits a random backoff.

cases.name: whole-seconds
cases.why: Whole seconds are waited exactly.

cases.name: zero-seconds
cases.why: Zero means retry at once.

cases.name: one-second
cases.why: One second is waited exactly.

cases.name: at-max-retry-delay
cases.why: A wait equal to maxRetryDelay is still waited.

cases.name: above-max-retry-delay
cases.why: A wait longer than maxRetryDelay is not retried; the call fails at once.

cases.name: far-above-max-retry-delay
cases.why: An hour is far beyond maxRetryDelay, so the call fails at once.

cases.name: beyond-64-bit-integers
cases.why: Seconds too large for a 64-bit integer still ask for longer than maxRetryDelay, so the call fails at once.

cases.name: leading-zeros
cases.why: Delay-seconds are one or more ASCII digits, so 007 waits seven seconds.

cases.name: only-zeros
cases.why: Several zeros are still digits, so 000 retries at once.

cases.name: empty
cases.why: An empty value is neither seconds nor a date, so it is ignored and the SDK backs off as if it were absent.

cases.name: negative-seconds
cases.why: A minus sign is not a digit, so -5 is ignored and the SDK backs off as if it were absent.

cases.name: plus-sign
cases.why: A plus sign is not a digit, so +5 is ignored and the SDK backs off as if it were absent.

cases.name: plus-sign-above-max-retry-delay
cases.why: An ignored value never fails the call, even one that would read as longer than maxRetryDelay.

cases.name: decimal-seconds
cases.why: A fraction is not delay-seconds, so 1.5 is ignored and the SDK backs off as if it were absent.

cases.name: junk-word
cases.why: A word is neither seconds nor a date, so the SDK backs off.

cases.name: junk-seconds-with-unit
cases.why: Seconds with a unit are not delay-seconds, so the SDK backs off.

cases.name: junk-truncated-date
cases.why: A date without its time is not an HTTP date, so the SDK backs off.

cases.name: imf-fixdate-future
cases.why: An IMF-fixdate five seconds ahead waits five seconds.

cases.name: imf-fixdate-at-max-retry-delay
cases.why: A date exactly maxRetryDelay ahead is still waited.

cases.name: imf-fixdate-above-max-retry-delay
cases.why: A date a minute ahead is beyond maxRetryDelay, so the call fails at once.

cases.name: imf-fixdate-now
cases.why: A date equal to now waits nothing.

cases.name: imf-fixdate-past
cases.why: A date already passed waits nothing.

cases.name: rfc-850-future
cases.why: The obsolete RFC 850 form is an HTTP date that recipients accept.

cases.name: rfc-850-past
cases.why: An RFC 850 date already passed waits nothing.

cases.name: rfc-850-above-max-retry-delay
cases.why: An RFC 850 date a minute ahead is beyond maxRetryDelay, so the call fails at once.

cases.name: asctime-future
cases.why: The obsolete asctime form, with a space-padded day, is an HTTP date that recipients accept.

cases.name: asctime-past
cases.why: An asctime date already passed waits nothing.

cases.name: asctime-above-max-retry-delay
cases.why: An asctime date five minutes ahead is beyond maxRetryDelay, so the call fails at once.

cases.name: asctime-two-digit-day-past
cases.why: An asctime date with a two-digit day the day before waits nothing.

cases.name: backoff-retry-0
cases.why: Full jitter before retry 0 waits from 0 up to min(8, 0.5 × 2^0) seconds.

cases.name: backoff-retry-1
cases.why: Full jitter before retry 1 waits from 0 up to min(8, 0.5 × 2^1) seconds.

cases.name: backoff-retry-2
cases.why: Full jitter before retry 2 waits from 0 up to min(8, 0.5 × 2^2) seconds.

cases.name: backoff-retry-3
cases.why: Full jitter before retry 3 waits from 0 up to min(8, 0.5 × 2^3) seconds.

cases.name: backoff-retry-4
cases.why: Full jitter before retry 4 waits from 0 up to min(8, 0.5 × 2^4) seconds.

cases.name: backoff-retry-5
cases.why: Full jitter before retry 5 waits from 0 up to min(8, 0.5 × 2^5) seconds.

cases.name: attempt-limits
cases.why: maxRetries 2 allows three attempts for retried failures, plus the one retry after a 401.

cases.name: retries-exhausted
cases.why: Two retries after the first attempt, then the last error.

cases.name: retries-then-success
cases.why: A success on the last allowed attempt answers it.

cases.name: every-retried-status
cases.why: 408, 429 and 504 are retried and share one budget.

cases.name: connection-and-timeout
cases.why: Connection failures and timeouts are retried.

cases.name: timeouts-exhausted
cases.why: The last attempt's failure is the error.

cases.name: not-retried-400
cases.why: 400 is never retried.

cases.name: not-retried-404
cases.why: 404 is never retried.

cases.name: not-retried-409
cases.why: 409 is never retried.

cases.name: not-retried-422
cases.why: 422 is never retried.

cases.name: not-retried-501
cases.why: 501 is not in the retried list.

cases.name: not-retried-505
cases.why: 505 is not in the retried list.

cases.name: redirect-not-followed
cases.why: A redirect is neither followed nor retried; it is an http_error.

cases.name: server-key-401-not-retried
cases.why: A server key cannot be refreshed, so a 401 fails at once.

cases.name: fixed-token-401-not-retried
cases.why: A fixed customer token cannot be refreshed, so a 401 fails at once.

cases.name: provider-401-retried-once
cases.why: A 401 asks the provider again and retries once.

cases.name: provider-401-twice
cases.why: Only one retry follows a 401; a second 401 fails.

cases.name: provider-503-401-200
cases.why: A retried failure then a 401 then success.

cases.name: provider-most-attempts
cases.why: The 401 retry is outside the budget, so maxRetries 2 allows four attempts.

cases.name: provider-401-after-budget
cases.why: A 401 after the budget is spent still has its one retry.

cases.name: provider-budget-spent-before-401
cases.why: The call fails once the budget is spent, before any later 401.

cases.name: provider-403-credential-not-allowed
cases.why: 403 credential_not_allowed is never retried or refreshed.

error.message: This route does not take this kind of credential.

cases.name: no-retries-allowed
cases.why: maxRetries 0 makes one attempt.

cases.name: no-retries-401-still-retried
cases.why: maxRetries 0 still allows the retry after a 401.

cases.name: no-retries-most-attempts
cases.why: maxRetries 0 allows at most two attempts.

cases.name: retry-after-above-max-not-retried
cases.why: A Retry-After beyond maxRetryDelay fails at once.

cases.name: retry-after-within-max-retried
cases.why: A Retry-After within maxRetryDelay is waited, then retried.

cases.name: write-retries-exhausted
cases.why: Writes are retried like reads, every attempt with the same Idempotency-Key, which the error carries.

cases.name: provider-401-then-503s
cases.why: The retry after a 401 goes at once and uses neither the budget nor a backoff step, so the next waits are retries 0 and 1.

cases.name: provider-401-then-503s-then-success
cases.why: After the immediate retry for a 401, both budgeted retries remain and back off from retry 0.

cases.name: provider-401-between-backoffs
cases.why: A 401 between backoffs goes at once and does not advance n, so the waits after it are retries 1 and 2.

cases.name: provider-401-then-retry-after
cases.why: The retry after a 401 goes at once, and a later Retry-After is waited exactly.

cases.name: retry-after-then-backoff
cases.why: A retry that waited for Retry-After is still retry 0, so the next backoff is retry 1's.

cases.name: retry-after-leading-zeros-waited
cases.why: Retry-After 007 is seven seconds, waited exactly.

cases.name: retry-after-negative-ignored
cases.why: An unreadable Retry-After is ignored, so the retry backs off as retry 0.

cases.name: retry-after-plus-sign-ignored
cases.why: An unreadable Retry-After never fails the call; the retry backs off as if it were absent.

cases.name: retry-after-past-date-retried-at-once
cases.why: A Retry-After date already passed waits nothing.

cases.name: answer-cut-off-retried
cases.why: An answer cut off while it is read is a ConnectionError, so it is retried like one.

cases.name: answers-cut-off-exhausted
cases.why: Answers cut off on every attempt spend the retries and fail with the last ConnectionError.
